subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: Acme ML / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reeves <jordan@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + sizing questions (Dedicated)

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can get you a firm Dedicated estimate: 

- Use case: product search + summarization + assisted authoring (mix of short and long responses).
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (you mentioned data isolation is required).
- Timeline: pilot in ~6 weeks, production in Q3 if pilot looks good.

A few sizing/qualification questions we need to confirm:
1) Expected sustained TPS and peak TPS (transactions per second) for inference?
2) Peak concurrent user requests we should plan for (concurrency)?
3) Typical token mix per request (prompt vs completion). Example: 300 prompt tokens / 700 completion tokens = 1,000 total.
4) Model family and size(s) you expect to run (e.g., Mistral 7B, Llama2 13B, MPT, proprietary).
5) Any strict latency SLOs (p95/p99) we should optimize for?
6) Do you expect long KV cache retention needs (multi-turn chat) or mostly stateless one-offs?

If you can send the brief workload spreadsheet you mentioned on the call (sample TPS by endpoint, token distribution, and a small prompt set), Rafael and I will run a quick capacity runbook and put together a baseline Recommended Configuration + cost estimate.

Next steps I propose:
- You: share the sizing spreadsheet and any sample prompts (Drive link is fine).
- Us: return a preliminary node-level config + estimate within 3 business days.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

--
Marissa Cole
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Reeves <jordan@acme-ml.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + sizing questions (Dedicated)
Attachments: acme-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (xlsx, 54KB)

Hi Marissa — thanks, great summary. Attaching the spreadsheet with our current traffic profile and token breakdown. High-level answers below: 

- Sustained TPS (avg): 8-12 TPS across our production cluster.
- Peak TPS: up to ~18 TPS for short spikes (marketing events).
- Peak concurrency: typical concurrency 4-6, spike concurrency up to 10.
- Token mix (approx avg per inference): prompt ~350 tokens, completion ~650 tokens => ~1,000 tokens total.
- Model mix: mostly Mistral 7B for lower-latency endpoints (~70% traffic) and Llama-2 13B for higher-quality summarization and fine-tuned flows (~30%).
- Latency SLO: target p95 < 300ms for Mistral flows; for 13B summarization we accept up to 1s p95 but prefer lower.
- KV cache: multi-turn retention for chat-like flows (approximately 20% of requests keep a session >5 turns).
- VPC/Isolation: yes - required for compliance.
- Timeline: pilot start early April, production September (flexible).

Drive link to prompts and sample traces: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeSamplePrompts

Let us know if you need any more detail.

- Jordan
Director of ML Engineering | Acme ML
jordan@acme-ml.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reeves <jordan@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + sizing questions (Dedicated)
Attachments: redwood-prelim-estimate.pdf (pdf, 28KB)

Thanks Jordan — that spreadsheet is perfect. Rafael/Aditya, copied to keep you in the loop.

Initial read: with an average of 10 TPS and ~1k tokens per request, the heavy Llama-2 13B traffic (~30%) pushes memory/compute requirements. Preliminary recommendation attached (high-level):
- Baseline: 4x A100-80GB (reserved) mapped as the committed pool to cover sustained 8-12 TPS with batching and KV caching optimizations.
- Burst: 2x additional A100 or A10G for short marketing spikes (automated burst pool).
- If you commit to H100 we can reduce node count for 13B, but A100 gives a cost/perf sweet spot for mixed workloads.
- Config tuning: aggressive batching for Mistral endpoints, per-route batching thresholds, and a 20s KV cache retention for multi-turn flows.

I attached a preliminary estimate showing monthly cost range for the baseline + burst and an initial SKU layout. This is a starting point - Rafael, can you validate performance assumptions and whether H100 should be recommended given their 13B runs?

Jordan - if that aligns, next steps would be:
1) Rafael to validate perf assumptions and propose node types.
2) We provide a formal Dedicated quote (PO-ready) and a mutual action plan for pilot.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Reeves <jordan@acme-ml.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + sizing questions (Dedicated)

Thanks for the detail - good baseline. A few technical notes from the infra side: 
- For the mixed Mistral 7B / Llama-2 13B workload you described, H100 provides the best density for 13B FP16/quantized runs, but the cost delta vs A100 may not be justified if 13B is only 30% of traffic. If Acme is sensitive to unit cost, A100-80GB nodes with optimized kernels and 4-bit quantization on 13B give a strong compromise.
- Suggested baseline config to start testing: 3x A100-80GB + 1x H100 (reserved) - H100 serves the heavy 13B bursts and reduces observed p95 for summarization flows. Keep 2x A10G as burst nodes for short spikes (lower-cost for Mistral).
- Concurrency: plan for 6 concurrent long-running summarization requests on the H100; batching will be tuned per route to keep p95 targets.
- KV cache: for multi-turn chat, plan for a modest KV eviction policy (20-60s depending on session patterns). We'll need sample prompt sets to estimate effective cache hit-rate.
- Next step: run a small perf test with your sample prompts and 1-2 representative models. Can we get: (a) 200-300 sample requests (varied token lengths) and (b) a short list of 3 production endpoints we should emulate?

If you send those, we can spin a perf run in ~5 business days and confirm node mix + throughput estimates and update the quote.

- Rafael
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Reeves <jordan@acme-ml.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + sizing questions (Dedicated)

Perfect - thanks, all. I uploaded a small sample set and 3 endpoint definitions to the Drive folder (same link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeSamplePrompts. Files include: sample-requests.csv, endpoint-defs.yaml, and traces-log.json.

We reviewed the preliminary estimate internally and prefer to start with the A100-first approach (3x A100 + 1x H100 + burst A10G) you suggested. Please go ahead with the perf run and share results. Also, we may need a PO for pilot (30-day term) - can you send the PO template and any standard contract terms?

Jordan Reeves
Director of ML Engineering | Acme ML
jordan@acme-ml.com
